anomalies.observed: On the EPD_Driver sheet the 24-pin FPC connector J6 (FH34SRJ-24S-0.5SH(99)) carries no-connect (X) markers on its pins 2 and 3, so the gate-drive (GDR) and current-sense (RESE) lines of the panel are not wired to the external boost stage: Q2 (MCH3478-TL-W) gate pin and the Q2-source/R2(0.47 ohm) sense node do not reach the connector.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires the boost MOSFET gate to be driven by the panel's GDR pin (J1.2) and the source/sense node to feed back to the panel's RESE pin (J1.3), closing the booster control loop inside the EPD module.

evidence.quote: EPD_Driver sheet: J6 FH34SRJ-24S pins 2 and 3 show no-connect (X) markers; Q2 (MCH3478-TL-W) gate and R2 0.47ohm source node are not connected to the connector.

Q1's gate (Net-(Q1-G)) is driven from J1.2 - the EPD panel's own GDR pin ... Q1's source (Net-(Q1-S)) returns through R1 (0.47 ohm) to GND and also feeds back to J1.3 (RESE, the panel's current-sense/booster-control input), closing the control loop entirely within the EPD module and external power stage.

anomalies.impact: With GDR and RESE left open, the panel's COG driver cannot control the external boost MOSFET, so the charge-pump/multiplier never generates the high voltages and the e-paper display will not power up (blank display).

parsed.summary: Reference designators differ from the spec throughout (a labeling convention, not a fault), but the EPD boost-converter control loop is broken: the schematic places no-connect markers on the FPC connector's GDR (pin 2) and RESE (pin 3) pins, leaving the MCH3478 gate and the 0.47-ohm sense node unconnected to the panel, which contradicts the spec's required booster feedback path and would prevent the display from powering up.
